clue.text: Worry, but finally getting money in Moscow

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the end of the word but
the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: Someone frets about cash, but finally gets paid in Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to trouble someone and to worry them both mean to disturb or upset them.

clue.text: Eleven, so tea gets made at the outset

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of made

explanation.surface: A cricket eleven breaks for tea, which gets brewed right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven is the number of players in a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A side of eleven players in cricket or football is a sporting group, so the number stands for the whole squad.

clue.text: One's mate running rings round parish priest

indicators.note: to run rings round something is to circle it, so the rings sit on either side of what follows

parts.note: two rings are two round O letters
PP is the standard abbreviation for parish priest

explanation.surface: A companion outwits the local vicar at every turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The two O letters split, one before and one after the PP.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is informal British slang for a colleague, partner or opposite number, someone's close companion.

clue.text: Brother with superior laugh makes a commotion

parts.note: bro is informal for brother
U means upper-class, socially superior
the sound of laughing

explanation.surface: A sibling's smug cackle causes a family row.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class comes from the old British 'U and non-U' distinction in speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or uproar over something, much the same as a commotion.

clue.text: Former spouse to take steps to be accurate

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
to act is to take steps or measures

explanation.surface: A divorced partner makes moves to get the record straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and accurate are adjectives that both describe something precise and correct in every detail.

clue.text: Border has order, but is lacking a plan

parts.note: a rand is a border or edge, such as a strip of leather on a shoe
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A frontier is neatly kept, yet nobody had any real strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random happens without method or design, made by chance rather than by any scheme.

clue.text: Something done for the first person in Acton

indicators.note: in places the person inside the name of the place

parts.note: taken as written; Acton is a district of west London
the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A deed performed for the leading resident of a London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a deed or act, literally a thing that has been carried out.

clue.text: Tack attaching your own number to sketch

indicators.note: attaching one thing to another joins them end to end

parts.note: a sketch is a rough drawing
a PIN is a personal identification number

explanation.surface: A tack is used to fix one's personal number to a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawing pin is the British name for a thumbtack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a short sharp nail, and a drawing pin is the flat-headed kind pushed into a noticeboard.

clue.text: Emma and Ann get new bosses

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women in an office receive replacement supervisors.
explanation.definitionFit: The management of a firm is its body of senior people in charge, collectively the ones running things.

clue.text: Thumbs up for a friend embracing hooker at five o'clock

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms around, so the friend surrounds what follows

parts.note: taken as written
a pal is a friend
pro is slang for a prostitute
on a clock face the five is marked with the Roman numeral V

explanation.surface: A mate gets the nod for meeting a working girl at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At five o'clock' reads as a time of day, but the solver must picture the clock face, where five is marked in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the thumbs up is a gesture of consent, so as a noun it means approval or endorsement.

clue.text: Try hard to type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: make a great effort, as a verb
second meaning: a variety or breed, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like advice to a slow typist; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means exert oneself greatly; as a noun it means a breed, variety or kind.

clue.text: Second child goes to toilet when held up in coach

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
CH is a standard abbreviation for child

indicators.note: in a down light, holding something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A child visits the lavatory while the bus is stuck in traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone and to coach them are verbs that both mean train or instruct.

clue.text: Question for the chef or planner

definitions.text: Question for the chef or planner

parts.note: surface reading: asking a cook what is on the stove tonight
setter's reading: asking someone scheming what they are up to

explanation.walkthrough: The informal phrase literally asks what food is on the heat, and idiomatically asks what is going on or being plotted.
explanation.definitionFit: The casual question is asked literally of a cook at the stove and figuratively of anyone hatching a scheme.

clue.text: Any girl not going astray is without intelligence

indicators.note: things going astray wander off their proper course, so the letters scatter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral warning: a girl who stays on the straight path lacks wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting ignorantly means acting in a way that shows no knowledge or understanding, an adverb of folly.

clue.text: How to abuse those roues in the Treasury

indicators.note: to abuse something is to mistreat or misuse it, knocking the letters out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A manual on mistreating rakes who work in the government finance department.
explanation.walkthrough: A roué is a debauched man, a rake.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is a place where riches are kept, so it is a kind of depository or repository for valuables.

clue.text: Be dismissed from the butcher's?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lose one's job, idiomatically

definitions.note: describes buying a cut of meat rather than giving a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally obtain a cut of meat at the shop

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading: a customer collecting a pork cutlet from the butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being fired from work also literally describes collecting a cutlet of lamb or pork.

clue.text: One hundred to go to the Bar, being talented

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: A gifted student heads off to train as a barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to the Bar' suggests becoming a lawyer; here the bar is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and talented are adjectives that both describe someone gifted, quick and able.

clue.text: Sticky substance makes a fool turn back

indicators.note: turning back means facing the other way, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a fool

explanation.surface: Something tacky causes a dupe to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is a glue or a resin, and in general any adhesive, tacky material.

clue.text: Someone laughing loudly at a sensational headline!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person howling with laughter
second meaning: journalists' slang for a lurid headline

explanation.surface: A reader roars with mirth at a lurid tabloid front page.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who screams with laughter is one sense; newspaper slang for a big, shocking headline is the other.

clue.text: Decapitated boar with blade

indicators.note: to decapitate is to cut off the head, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A beheaded wild pig lies beside a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of a rowing oar is called the blade, and by extension the whole oar is a blade in rowing slang.

clue.text: Thought what Narcissus fell in love with

definitions.text: what Narcissus fell in love with
definitions.meaning: second meaning: his own image in a pool

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Narcissus fell for his own image seen in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious consideration is one sense; the mirrored image in still water that the mythical youth adored is the other.

clue.text: Produced replicas of 151 diamonds

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals, plus one
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller made copies of a large batch of gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloned means made identical genetic or exact copies, so it is a past-tense verb for duplicating.

clue.text: Weakness shown when she cuts a cold fish?

parts.note: taken as written
a chill is coldness

indicators.note: something that cuts into a thing slices its way inside it

parts.note: an eel is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook reveals her soft spot when slicing up a cold fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Achilles was invulnerable except at the heel by which his mother held him when dipping him in the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero was invulnerable except at one spot on his foot, so the phrase means a fatal vulnerability.

clue.text: Ex-PM to dine inside two hours

indicators.note: inside places the eating within the pair of hours

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hour, twice
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A former prime minister takes a two-hour lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath led the British government as Conservative premier in the early 1970s, so he is a former holder of the office.

clue.text: Sketch of soprano with clothes on

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music
kit is clothing, and on says it is placed after in a down light

explanation.surface: A short comic turn about a singer who keeps her costume on.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch or parody performed on stage or screen.

clue.text: So what can be found in "Mother Goose"?

indicators.note: what can be found in a phrase is tucked inside it, spanning the words

parts.note: the end of Mother and the start of Goose

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks what is in a book of nursery rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is the Latin for therefore, so as a conjunction it carries the logical sense of so.

clue.text: Endlessly faithful worker? But he hasn't turned up

definitions.note: a clause describing the person, standing for the noun

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: true means faithful or loyal
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A loyal employee seems endlessly dependable, yet fails to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is someone, usually a pupil, who stays away from school without leave and so is absent.

clue.text: Grass producer facing quite a blow

parts.note: hay is dried grass
a maker is one who produces

explanation.surface: A farmer growing grass gets a nasty knock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass producer' looks like a definition itself, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a wild, swinging punch, so it is a heavy knockout strike in boxing slang.

clue.text: Crops obtained from Disley

indicators.note: obtained from says the letters are taken out and worked into something new

parts.note: taken as written; Disley is a village in Cheshire

explanation.surface: A harvest gathered from farms around an English village.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm's yields are its harvests, the amount of produce it brings in, plural nouns like crops.

clue.text: Hamlet's friend taking half an hour over correspondence

indicators.note: half a word keeps just one of its two halves, here the front

parts.note: the front pair of letters
a ratio is a correspondence or proportion between quantities

explanation.surface: A prince's companion spends thirty minutes on his letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Correspondence suggests letters, but here it means a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is the loyal friend of the prince in Shakespeare's tragedy, the one who survives to tell his story.
